summary.title: The 14 pains of building your own billing system
summary.one_liner: Building billing in-house runs into 14 recurring problems (idempotency, proration, tax, invoicing, revenue recognition and more), so the author argues you should buy an off-the-shelf billing system.
takeaways: Billing touches finance, product, support, legal, compliance and sales, so it is much harder than an engineering-only task.
The three common patterns are home-grown, full third-party, or a hybrid, each with trade-offs in control versus cost.
Key pain points include idempotency, date handling, proration, usage metering, multi-country tax and invoice formats, and revenue recognition.
Tax rules and invoice formats change often and grow with scale, while idempotency is usually solved once.
The author recommends buying billing software (naming Solvimon, Orb, Lago) and focusing engineering on usage events and product-specific lifecycle logic.
summary.summary: This opinion essay by Arnon Shimoni argues that building your own billing system is far harder than it looks. It compares three approaches (home-grown, full third-party, and hybrid) in a table and then lists 14 problem areas, ordered from least to most complex, such as idempotency, date handling, proration, usage metering, tax, invoice formatting, customer hierarchies, refunds, custom deals, and revenue recognition. A grid maps each problem by how often it changes and how much it is affected by scale. The author concludes by recommending off-the-shelf billing tools, naming Solvimon, Orb, and Lago, and keeping in-house effort on product-specific usage and lifecycle events.
